name: Boundary Waters Canoe Area
unique: A million acres of glacier carved lakes where motors are banned, portages are measured in rods and the only way in is a paddle.
buzz: People call it the best wilderness trip in the lower 48; permits are limited and mosquitoes are a force of nature. Book permits in January.

name: Drive a Tank
unique: An armoured vehicle park where you can drive a real tank, crush a car and fire a machine gun, run by people who take safety and fun equally seriously.
buzz: It is expensive and completely unforgettable; the car crush package is the one people book. Reservations required.

name: Minneapolis Institute of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Asian art, African art, photography and a period room collection.
buzz: Free and excellent, with a good cafe and a strong Asian collection. A full afternoon.

name: Paisley Park
unique: Prince's private compound, preserved almost exactly as he left it: the soundstage, the vault, the purple corridor and the doves.
buzz: Fans call it moving and slightly eerie; the general tour is short and the VIP tour gets into the studio. Book ahead.

name: Guthrie Theater
unique: A major regional theater with three stages and a cantilevered lobby over the Mississippi, founded by Tyrone Guthrie.
buzz: The building and the river view are worth the visit, and the productions are strong. Rush tickets exist.

name: Minnesota State Fair
unique: The largest state fair in the country by attendance, with 500 food vendors, a butter sculpture of Princess Kay and a crop art competition that is a genuine art form.
buzz: The food on a stick innovation is real; the Sweet Martha's cookie bucket is a ritual. Go on a weekday and split everything.

name: Split Rock Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse on a cliff above Lake Superior, built after a 1905 storm wrecked a fleet, with keeper's quarters and a film.
buzz: The cliff setting is dramatic and the tour is good. Go on a clear day for the lake color.

name: Voyageurs National Park
unique: A water based national park of lakes and islands on the Canadian border, reached by boat, with loons, eagles and dark skies.
buzz: You need a boat or a tour, and that keeps it quiet. The fall colors and the northern lights are the reward.

name: Grand Marais and the Gunflint Trail
unique: A harbor town at the edge of the Boundary Waters with a 57 mile road into the lakes, a donut shop and a coastline of basalt and birch.
buzz: The Gunflint Trail and the harbor are the two reasons to come and the fall color is the season; the town is small and the wilderness starts immediately.

name: Itasca State Park
unique: The headwaters of the Mississippi, where you can wade across the river, plus old growth pine and a lodge.
buzz: Walking across the Mississippi is the photo and the park is beautiful. The lodge is a good base.

name: Minnehaha Falls
unique: A 53 foot waterfall in a city park, with trails down to the creek and a seafood shack at the top.
buzz: The falls are easy to reach and the park is lovely. The Sea Salt eatery is the local lunch.

name: Minnesota Landscape Arboretum
unique: One thousand two hundred acres of display gardens, prairie and woods with a three mile drive, a sculpture garden and a bog walk.
buzz: The azalea and hosta collections are the summer draws and the winter lights are the local tradition; the drive loop is the easy way to see it.

name: Walker Art Center
unique: A contemporary art center with a sculpture garden across the street, including the Spoonbridge and Cherry.
buzz: The sculpture garden is free and the Spoonbridge is the photo. The museum is for contemporary tastes.

name: Gooseberry Falls
unique: A triple waterfall on the Gooseberry River dropping into Lake Superior, with a trail along the gorge and pink granite shorelines nearby.
buzz: Easy access and big payoff; it is crowded in summer. The Lake Superior shoreline at Split Rock is the bonus stop.

name: Canal Park
unique: A lakefront district with a lift bridge, a maritime museum, a beach and a pier where ore boats pass through.
buzz: The lift bridge and the ships are the draw, and the lake walk is windy and beautiful.

name: Como Park Zoo and Conservatory
unique: A free zoo and conservatory with polar bears, gorillas, a Japanese garden and a carousel.
buzz: Free and genuinely good for families, with the conservatory as the winter escape.

name: Glensheen Mansion
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 39 room Jacobean mansion on Lake Superior with original furnishings and a carriage house, and the story of a 1977 murder that still draws visitors.
buzz: The house and the lake setting are the tour and the crime story is the hook; the full mansion tour is worth the upgrade.

name: Interstate Park at Taylors Falls
unique: The oldest state park in the country, with basalt cliffs above the St. Croix, glacial potholes and a boat tour through the Dalles.
buzz: The pothole trail and the cliff overlooks are the walks and the river boat is the family option; the cliffs are popular with climbers.

name: Science Museum of Minnesota
unique: A science museum with a dinosaur hall, a Mississippi River exhibit, a omnitheater and a cell lab.
buzz: The river exhibit and the dinosaurs are the highlights. Good for a rainy day.

name: Tettegouche State Park
unique: North Shore cliffs and waterfalls on the Baptism River, with a sea cave, a suspension bridge and trails to a high overlook of Lake Superior.
buzz: TheShovel Point trail and the High Falls are the two walks; the park is busy in fall and the lake is cold year round.

name: Judge C.R. Magney State Park
unique: The Devil's Kettle, where half of the Brule River disappears into a hole in the rock, with a trail along the river and a staircase down to the falls.
buzz: The disappearing river is the mystery and the trail is 1.5 miles; the staircase is steep and the park is on the North Shore.

name: National Eagle Center
unique: A center on the Mississippi with resident bald and golden eagles, a viewing deck over the river and winter eagle counts that reach hundreds.
buzz: The resident eagles are close and the staff explain their injuries; the winter viewing deck is the season for wild birds.

name: St. Paul Winter Carnival
unique: An 1886 festival built to prove winter is survivable, with an ice palace, snow sculpting competition, parades and a Vulcan Krewe that has to be seen.
buzz: The ice palace is the draw in years it is built; the parade is genuinely fun. Dress for -10 and embrace it.

name: Mayo Clinic Tour
unique: A guided tour of the clinic's campus and history, from the 1889 Saint Marys Hospital to the modern Gonda building and the art collection inside.
buzz: The art and the architecture are the surprises and the guides explain the Mayo brothers' model; the tour is free but needs booking.

name: Minneopa State Park
unique: A double waterfall on the Blue Earth River and a bison drive through prairie, on the edge of Mankato.
buzz: The falls are a short walk and the bison are visible from the road; the park is small and the falls are best after rain.

name: Munsinger Gardens
unique: A formal garden on the Mississippi with beds of annuals, a lily pond and a greenhouse, next to the wilder Clemens Garden.
buzz: The display beds are the reason gardeners come and it is free; the river setting and the shade make it a summer afternoon.

name: SPAM Museum
unique: A free museum devoted to a canned meat product, with a production line, a world map of SPAM love and a tasting counter where you can try flavors sold nowhere else.
buzz: It is free, well made and genuinely funny; the tasting is the highlight. A perfect road trip break.

name: Stillwater Lift Bridge
unique: A 1931 vertical lift bridge over the St. Croix, now a pedestrian and bike crossing between Minnesota and Wisconsin, with a historic main street on each side.
buzz: The walk across the bridge is the easy pleasure and the river town is the rest; the bridge is closed to cars and open to bikes.

name: Quarry Park and Nature Preserve
unique: Abandoned granite quarries filled with clear water, with swimming holes, cliffs and trails through the stone piles.
buzz: The quarry swimming is the local summer ritual and the water is cold and deep; the county limits access and the cliffs are dangerous.

name: Great Lakes Aquarium
unique: The only freshwater aquarium in the country, with a walk through tunnel under Lake Superior fish, otters and a river otter slide.
buzz: The otters and the tunnel are the family stops and the freshwater focus makes it different from a coastal aquarium; it is on the Duluth harbor.

name: Mall of America
unique: An indoor amusement park with a log flume and roller coasters in the middle of a shopping mall, plus an aquarium and a LEGO store.
buzz: The park is better than it has any right to be; it is a suburban temple of consumerism and kids love it. Weekdays are calmer.

name: Minnesota Zephyr
unique: A dinner train along the St. Croix valley in restored 1940s cars, leaving from a Stillwater depot.
buzz: The dome car and the river view are the reason to ride and the brunch run is the family one; book ahead for the fall color weekends.

name: Quarry Hill Nature Center
unique: A nature center built into a limestone quarry with trails through oak woods, a cave and a pond, free and open to the public.
buzz: The cave and the trails are good with children and it is free; the center has live animals and a bird viewing room.

name: Hubbard House
customer: House tour people, local history fans, families
unique: A brick Italianate house built by a railroad builder, furnished with the family's belongings and a carriage house in the yard.
buzz: The volunteers know the family and the house is a step back; it is small and the tour is an hour.
